channel.title: Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty (rferl.org)

item.title: How Russia Is Recruiting Central Asian Women For Its War In Ukraine
item.description: Thousands of Central Asians are believed to have joined Russia’s war effort in Ukraine, including women who were coerced or lured by offers of lucrative jobs.

item.title: Once Washington's Closest Caucasus Partner, Georgia To Watch Vance Visit From The Outside
item.description: Once Washington’s closest partner in the South Caucasus, Georgia now finds itself stranded in US regional diplomacy. And as Tbilisi deepens ties with China while maintaining its engagement with Russia, Washington’s attention is increasingly shifting toward Azerbaijan and Armenia.

item.title: Russian Orthodox Church In US Sees 'Amazing Change' As New Converts Join
item.description: At a Russian Orthodox Church in Washington DC, church leaders say they've seen a significant rise in attendance from newcomers hoping to join the congregation. Many of the new converts have no initial family ties to Orthodox Christianity and discovered the faith through social media channels.

item.title: From Antarctica To The Front Lines: Ukraine's 'Military Penguins'
item.description: A small but growing contingent of Ukrainians have become veterans both of Ukraine's only Antarctic base, and the battle against the Russian invasion.

item.title: Live Blog: Trump, Netanyahu Set To Discuss Talks With Iran
item.description: Thousands of Iranians are dead or detained in a brutal crackdown after they took to the streets in what is seen as the biggest threat to the Islamic regime in years. Journalists from RFE/RL’s Iranian service, Radio Farda, bring you the latest developments, analysis, and reporting from on the ground.

item.title: Russia Accuses Ukrainian Intelligence Of Plot To Assassinate Top General
item.description: Russia officials said the man they identified as the gunman who shot the No. 2 general in the Russian military intelligence agency purportedly told them he was recruited by Ukrainian intelligence.

item.title: Kites Return To The Skies Of Lahore After A 19-Year Ban
item.description: Kites have once again filled the skies of the Pakistani city of Lahore after a 19-year ban. Markets sold thousands of handmade kites in the colors of spring flowers to eager flyers who often compete in aerial "battles" by trying to slice rivals' kite strings.

item.title: Iran Launches Crackdown On Reformist Politicians After Mass Protests
item.description: Iran has arrested several prominent reformist politicians as the authorities widen their crackdown on dissent following mass anti-government protests that posed one of the biggest threats to the clerical establishment in years.

item.title: Vance Arrives In Armenia As US Looks To Consolidate Caucasus Peace Plan
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance arrived in Armenia on February 9 to kick off a four-day visit to the Caucasus in support of a US-brokered peace deal and to push a strategic transit corridor Washington sees as central to reshaping trade, energy, and influence in the region.

item.title: 'If I Die': Loyal Dog Mourns At Iranian Protester's Graveside
item.description: Alireza Karami is one of the victims who died during Iran's violent crackdown on anti-regime protests. The image of his loyal dog at his graveside, has gained widespread attention on social media. Before his death, the 26-year-old auto body repairman left a touching testament for his beloved pet.
